main_topics.reason: The user repeatedly asked how to choose and sequence RA treatment around trying for a baby in one to two years.
The user said their rheumatologist had started methotrexate and asked whether being on it now was concerning.
The user recognized they needed to avoid pregnancy while taking methotrexate after the assistant raised contraception.
The user asked what could happen if a pregnancy-compatible medication controlled their RA less well than methotrexate.
The user asked whether RA symptoms change during pregnancy and noted they wanted to prepare for possible postpartum flares.
The user asked whether pregnancy-compatible medicines were also compatible with breastfeeding.
The user asked which clinicians to involve and whether to raise pregnancy plans with the rheumatologist now.
The user described starting out anxious about having to choose between their health and having a baby, then said they felt more in control.

output.summary: Recently diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis and taking methotrexate, the user sought a plan for medication choices while hoping to try for a baby in one to two years, including treatment transitions, pregnancy, postpartum, and breastfeeding. The assistant answered their questions and suggested discussing plans with the rheumatologist and an obstetrician; the user confirmed the recap, planned to raise it at their next visit, and said they felt less anxious and more in control.
